transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you and what brings you in today?

I guess what’s been bothering me is my eating after my evening class. Sometimes I’ll stop and get a full fast-food meal, then grab candy from a vending machine, and when I get home I keep going with more snacks. It feels like I’m making up for the whole day all at once.
After you eat like that, do you ever try to compensate by making yourself vomit, using laxatives, or exercising a lot more than usual?
Yeah… a few times after those late-night eating spells, I’ve gone to the bathroom and made myself throw up. I get scared that all that food is going to show on me, so I’ve done that.
How often have you had these episodes where you eat a lot and then try to compensate by making yourself throw up or other methods?
For about the last three months, it’s been usually once a week after class. I’ll overeat like that, and then afterward I make myself throw up.
When you're eating like that, do you feel like you can't control how much you're eating or stop yourself once you start?

Yeah, I do. Once I start on the snacks, I’ll tell myself to just close the bag and go to bed, but I don’t. I keep reaching for more, like I’m not really stopping myself, and then I end up feeling embarrassed and kind of sick of myself.
Do these episodes of overeating usually happen after you feel particularly stressed, upset, or in response to something emotional, or do they happen more spontaneously without a clear trigger?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed one clear trigger every time. Sometimes I’m worn out or tense, but other times it just kind of happens when I’m by myself and start eating.
Outside of those evenings after class, do you ever have other times where you feel like you’re eating a lot again in a short period, even if you aren’t making yourself throw up afterward?

Yeah, sometimes. What actually got me worried is after my evening class I’ll stop for food and it turns into a lot — like a full fast-food meal, then candy from a vending machine, and then when I get home I’ll still eat more snacks. It feels like I’m making up for not eating much earlier in the day.
Besides making yourself throw up, have you used any other methods like fasting, extreme dieting, or taking diet pills to try to control your weight after these eating episodes?

I’m not sure. I mean, I’ve tried to not eat much earlier in the day sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I’m taking diet pills or doing anything planned like that. Mostly it’s just the throwing up that I’ve done.
Do you judge yourself or feel particularly bad about your body shape or weight after these eating episodes?

Yeah. I do judge myself after. Like, if my shirt feels tight around my stomach the next day, I get pretty down on myself. I feel like I failed at being careful or disciplined, even if everything else, like my work, is going fine.

Can you describe what happens during one of these episodes where you feel like you can't stop eating — how much do you typically eat, and do you feel like you're eating in a discrete period of time, like within a couple of hours?

Yeah, it’s usually all in one stretch. Like after class I’ll stop and get a full fast-food meal, and then I’ll still get candy from a vending machine. Then when I get home, I keep going with snacks. It feels like a lot for me, like I’m trying to make up for barely eating earlier in the day.
Would you say that how you see yourself or how you feel about yourself is strongly influenced by how you feel about your body shape or weight?

Yes, I’d say it does. If I feel like my shirt is tight around my middle, it really affects how I see myself. I start thinking I’ve failed at being careful or disciplined, even if everything else, like my bookkeeping work, is going okay.
Would you say that your sense of self-worth is strongly tied to how you feel about your body shape or weight?

Yes, I think it is. Like I said, if my shirt feels tight around my stomach or middle, it can make me feel like I’ve failed at being careful and disciplined. Even if my work is going fine, that feeling about my body can really bring me down.

During these episodes after your evening class, would you say that you're eating an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most people would eat in the same amount of time under similar circumstances?

Yes, I think so. It’s more than I’d normally expect someone to eat in that time. After class I might have a full fast-food meal, then candy from the vending machine, and when I get home I’ll still keep going with snacks, like I’m making up for not eating much all day.
Would you say that these episodes after your evening class, where you eat a lot in a short time, happen repeatedly and feel like they’re happening on their own without you planning them?

Yes. It does feel like it happens on its own. Once I start on those snacks, I’ll tell myself, okay, close the bag and just go to bed, but then my hands keep reaching for more. I don’t really plan it that way. I just keep going until I feel embarrassed and kind of sick of myself.
